payload.feature:
Two items on the egress axis (decision 0036, accepted 2026-09-03, enacted in #160). Read docs/decisions/0036-egress-is-a-property-of-the-route.md and the notes on PR #160 first. Nothing beyond these two items.

ITEM 1 — the queued MEDIUM security residual from #160's reviewer, fixed. In crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs the route resolver reads an inline seat's model pin through `model_pin(raw)`, which is `command_pin(raw, "--model", 80)`: the flag is hardcoded, but `model_flag` is per-adapter data (`Adapter.model_flag` in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents.rs; test fixtures already use "-m"). For an inline site on an adapter the operator ADDS whose flag is not `--model`, a route-prefixed pin reads as ModelPin::Absent, `resolve_route` treats it as the unprefixed case and hands the adapter's OWN class — the fail-open the decision's first rejected alternative describes, through a second door. The reviewer proved it: adapter `many` with egress "contracted", model_flag "-m", and an inline seat `[{brokkr},driver,many,--,-m,elsewhere/large-1]` declaring secrets compiled. Fix in `enforce_model_policy`: resolve the adapter FIRST, then read the pin with that adapter's declared `model_flag` (an adapter declaring "unsupported" has no pin to read and its unprefixed class applies); keep `command_pins_model` / the four built-ins (claude, lanetally, codex, dsh) on `--model` for decision 0031's pin refusal, which is a different rule. Turn the reviewer's probe into the test that trips before the fix and passes after, in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/model_policy_tests.rs, plus a test that an adapter with model_flag "unsupported" still resolves its unprefixed class and no better. Fix the code comment at the ruling-4 refusal that claims the `--model` case is the only door.

ITEM 2 — the operator's ruling, recorded as data. The operator ruled on 2026-09-03: the dsh route `spark` (the operator's own DGX Spark, http://spark:30000/v1, the SGLang server the profile names) is class `local` — the top of the ordered vocabulary. Enact it exactly as 0036 ruling 1 says class assignment is made: in adapters/dsh.json add `"routes": {"spark": "local"}` and `"credentials": {"spark": "SPARK_API_KEY"}` (the variable the profile says that route requires to be named; the server checks no key), leave dsh's own adapter-level class where it is (unprefixed dsh ids and every other route stay uncontracted), and append one dated line to the Ruling section of docs/decisions/0036-egress-is-a-property-of-the-route.md recording that the operator ruled spark local on 2026-09-03 and that no other route is classed. The migration test from #160 that pins the five adapters' clearances must be UPDATED to state the new spark truth, not weakened: dsh unprefixed → uncontracted, dsh dashscope/* → uncontracted, dsh spark/* → local. Every bundle that seats dsh (recipes/night-shift, recipes/wager-harness, and whatever else compiles it in) moves its digest because its `drivers` witness pins the adapter file; re-pin those witnesses in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/compose_tests.rs, only the ones that move, and say in the commit which moved and why. `brokkr doctor` on this workspace should now name the spark route's credential as ambient if SPARK_API_KEY is in the process environment and not in the bindings store.

Do not touch: the wire protocol, any journal row, the tier vocabulary, the trust tier of any adapter, decision 0021 rulings 2, 3 and 7, the two LOW riders from #160's notes (doctor's ambient check keying, route-prefix grammar) — those wait for their own ruling. Two commits are fine, one per item, each with its tests. Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included.

SECURITY RESIDUAL (low, unfixed) — command_pin's flag grammar leaves a narrower version of the door the fix closed. It recognizes only 'FLAG VALUE' and 'FLAG=VALUE'. For a short model_flag the standard getopt bare-attached form is neither. Proven empirically with a throwaway probe (since reverted; tree clean): on an adapter with egress 'contracted' and model_flag '-m', a secret-binding inline seat with argv '-melsewhere/large-1' COMPILES CLEAN, taking the adapter's contracted class while its argv names the unruled route 'elsewhere'. The '-m=elsewhere/large-1' spelling is correctly refused. Same fail-open shape as the fixed MEDIUM, same function, same population (operator-added adapters), different argv spelling.

Why low and not medium: zero exposure on the shipped tree — all five shipped adapters declare the long flag '--model', where '--model=X' is handled and '--modelX' is not a legal spelling. It requires the operator to add a short-flag adapter AND a bundle to use the attached form. The change is also a strict improvement: before it, EVERY spelling on a short-flag adapter was unread.

Why I did not fix it: the naive fix (strip_prefix on the bare flag) creates false pins — with flag '-m', an unrelated '-mode' would read as a pin 'ode'. Deciding what spellings a declared flag legally covers is flag/route-prefix grammar, which the task explicitly defers to its own ruling alongside #160's two LOW riders. Fixing it here would be me ruling on that.

Related, same family, recorded for whoever takes that ruling: an adapter declaring '-m' whose real CLI also accepts '--model' as an alias. A seat writing '--model route/x' reads Absent and inherits the adapter class. The new test codifies this as intended ('a flag this provider does not take pins nothing'), which is a defensible reading of model_flag as the single authoritative flag — but it is an assumption the grammar ruling should confirm, not an accident.

SIMPLICITY — nothing to raise. The adapter is looked up twice (once for the pin read, once in the loop); that duplication is forced by the &mut destructure and the two-arm match, and hoisting it would complicate the agent-chain arm for no gain. The unwrap_or("--model") in the Unreadable arm is unreachable by construction (an unsupported flag reads Absent) and its own comment says so; it is defensive, not dead policy.

Second implement visit. Items 1 and 2 were already delivered and committed on the first visit (52f8e04, 463737d) and this visit did not touch them; the review returned `residual` with one unfixed LOW security finding, and closing it is the whole of this commit.

The residual: `command_pin` reads two spellings, `FLAG VALUE` and `FLAG=VALUE`. For a SHORT `model_flag` the standard getopt form is neither — `-melsewhere/large-1` attaches the value to the flag. The read found no flag, called the site unpinned, and ruling 2 hands an unpinned site its adapter's own class. Same fail-open, same function, same population (an adapter the operator ADDS) as the MEDIUM item 1 fixed, reached by a spelling rather than by a key. I reproduced it as a test first: `a_value_written_onto_the_flag_itself_is_unread_and_never_unpinned` fails with 'expected a compile refusal' on the pre-commit tree and passes after — a real red/green, not a test written around the answer.

The fix: a word beginning with the declared flag that is neither the flag alone nor `flag=value` now reads `ModelPin::Unreadable`, the state that already means 'the flag is there and I cannot read it as one concrete value'. At the ruling-4 refusal that falls to the floor, so a secret-binding seat is refused and told which flag it tripped on. Also extended the ruling-4 block comment: the 'no second door' claim now covers the spelling as well as the key.

Why this is not the deferred grammar ruling. The reviewer declined the fix because the naive one (strip_prefix -> Concrete) invents pins out of unrelated words — `-march` under `-m` would pin `arch` — and deciding which spellings a flag legally covers is the route/flag grammar rider the framing defers. I did not decide that. Refusing to READ is not a grammar; it is the fail-closed posture the axis exists for, and it cuts both ways deliberately: `-mnearby/small-1` is refused too, though `nearby` is a route the fixture declares local. A reading that let that one through would be the grammar ruling taken quietly. The test asserts the refusal names illegibility ('on a destination it does not name'), not route 'elsewhere', so the record says what the compiler actually knows. The grammar question — what the attached spelling MEANS — is untouched and still waits for its ruling, as do the two LOW riders from #160.

RESIDUAL 1 — MEDIUM, SECURITY. bundle.rs:1229 / model_policy_tests.rs (`a_route_named_on_the_adapters_own_flag_is_the_route_that_is_read`, the `.expect("a flag this provider does not take pins nothing")` case). The fix keys the read to the ONE flag string the adapter declares, and the new test blesses the consequence: on an adapter declaring `model_flag: "-m"`, a secret-binding inline seat whose argv reads `--model elsewhere/large-1` now compiles CLEAN and is granted the adapter's own (contracted) class. Under the pre-run code that exact argv was refused (it read as `Concrete("elsewhere/large-1")` -> uncontracted), so this shape moved from refused to accepted. `model_flag` is the flag the adapter COMPOSES with, not an exhaustive statement of what the CLI accepts, and real model CLIs routinely accept both spellings (`-m`/`--model`). Failure scenario, sharpest form: operator adds adapter `many` (`model_flag: "-m"`, `egress: "contracted"`, `routes: {nearby: local}`); a seat binding `TOKEN` writes `[{brokkr},driver,many,--,-m,nearby/small-1,--model,elsewhere/large-1]`. The compiler reads `-m` -> `nearby` -> local -> passes the egress bar; the provider, honouring `--model` (or last-flag-wins), sends the material to `elsewhere`, a route nobody ruled on. Same fail-open as the queued #160 MEDIUM, one door over — the alias rather than the key. Not fixed here because deciding which spellings/aliases a declared flag covers IS the flag-grammar question the run deliberately deferred alongside #160's two LOW riders (see the `Unreadable`, not `Concrete` comment at bundle.rs:392); the honest fail-closed option is to treat a `--model`-shaped pin found on an adapter that declares a different flag as `Unreadable`, and that needs a ruling, not a reviewer's small safe fix. Queue it the way #160's was queued.

RESIDUAL 2 — LOW, correctness/scope, no security consequence (fail-closed direction). The new `else if part.starts_with(flag)` early return in `command_pin` (bundle.rs:381) is shared with `command_pins_model` and `command_pins_effort`, so it also changes what counts as a pinned argv for decision 0031 and 0035, which the task put out of scope. `["--model","sonnet","--model-fallback","opus"]` used to read `Concrete("sonnet")` and now reads `Unreadable`, i.e. a built-in seat that DOES state a concrete model would be refused by `collect_unpinned` as if it stated none, with a message that names the wrong problem. Exposure on the shipped tree is zero — all four model-bearing adapters declare `--model`, and I grepped recipes/, bundles/, agents/, adapters/ for any token beginning with `--model`/`--effort` that is not the flag itself: none — and the direction is fail-closed, which is why this is LOW and not a hold. But it is untested (no test covers the 0031 path with a flag-prefixed word), and 45a8d5a's commit message overstates it: "decision 0031's pin refusal and 0035's effort pin are untouched" is true only of today's data, not of the rule.

The conclusion it supports (zero exposure) still holds. Not worth rewriting history for; noted so the record is not relied on verbatim.

COMMITTED — 3b5970a, 'a neighbouring flag is not an illegible spelling'. Closes RESIDUAL 2 (LOW, correctness/scope). 45a8d5a put the strict unread-spelling reading into the SHARED walker `command_pin`, which serves three rulings, so it silently rewrote decisions 0031 and 0035 — flatly out of scope per the task's own non-goals ('do not touch command_pins_model / model_pin').
